(net 161))' -- starts exactly on the now-copper-less pad, length sqrt(0.005^2+0.025^2)=0.0255 mm, a real physical stub, not a counting artifact. w1_2's other two pads (L1 pin 4, RT1 pin 1) are unaffected THT pads with real copper. _march.2026-07-29-creepage-admitted: This is a ceiling repair for a gate that is red on main independent of any change in this commit: four consecutive unmodified-main samples measured aggregate 842 / clearance 499 / creepage 32, i.e. main's own error_ceiling of 820 was already stale before this commit existed. The '+340V_BUS' -> '+170V_BUS' netclass-key rename in this commit does NOT cause the 32 creepage violations -- they are present on unmodified main and the rename has zero measurable DRC impact on them; classifying the rail correctly does not change what kicad-cli measures on the board. creepage is added to violations_by_type at 32 (previously absent, i.e. an implicit ceiling of 0, which is why the aggregate was already failing) so the category is tracked explicitly instead of hiding inside an unlabeled aggregate gap. error_ceiling 820 -> 845 on explicit human approval (bennetleff, 2026-07-29): 842 (= 820 + 32, i.e. just adding the new creepage category to the existing aggregate) undercounted, because it implicitly credited clearance at its observed floor of 499 rather than its documented per-type ceiling. drc_ceiling.json's own 'clearance' entry already records the count as varying 499-501 across samples with a per-type ceiling of 502 (observed-max + 1 headroom, the same convention used throughout this file, e.g. the 2026-07-29-tank-cap-remeasure entry). Applying that same already-approved convention to the aggregate: 842 - 499 + 502 = 845. This is not new violation debt -- it is admitting an already-admitted category's known run-to-run variance into the aggregate so the gate does not flake the moment clearance reaches 501. Both 845 and creepage: 32 carry the Ceiling-Approval trailer on the landing commit. Both numbers remain debt against _goal error_ceiling: 0, not an accepted end state: the honest reading is that this board has 32 places where an HV creepage requirement is not met, invisible until measured this way. The rename's own value is separate and does not touch the ceiling: scripts/check_hv_netclass_coverage.py goes from 1 unclassified HV net to 0, so the +170V_BUS rail resolves to HighVoltage in the placer's model instead of silently falling through to the Default/LV path -- correctness of classification, not a cause of the creepage count.
